## 技术雷达 · 2026-11-27

今天最重要的变化，不是某个新模型，而是推理系统的优化重心同时向 **host 运行时、权重传输与稀疏注意力后端**延伸：vLLM 在 Blackwell 上把 QSA prefill 切到 FlashInfer，TTFT 显著下降；FlashInfer 压榨 NVFP4 MoE epilogue；TensorRT-LLM 处理 CPython 帧栈抖动；vLLM 新增 `sparse_disk` 权重更新后端。以下按证据强度分级分析。

---

### 1. FlashInfer：routed NVFP4 MoE GEMM1 epilogue 优化

- **原始材料**：[perf(moe): faster pre-FC2 GEMM1 epilogue (compact decode tiles, packed BF16 rounding)](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9848)，2026-11-25，GitHub PR。
- **试图解决的旧问题**：在 routed NVFP4 MoE 的 pre-FC2 路径中，GEMM1 的 epilogue 是每 tile 瓶颈：无论 tile 里 2 行有效还是 128 行有效，都会对全部 128 行执行 BF16 rounding、`tanh.approx`、`div.full` 与 FP4 量化，包括 padding rows，导致 GEMM1 实际带宽只有 3.07 TB/s，而 GEMM2 达 6.43 TB/s。
- **核心技术机制**：两条路径改造 epilogue，不改算法。一是 **compact decode tiles**：当 tile 有效行 ≤64 时，只对有效行 staging `bf16(alpha * acc)`，128 个 epilogue 线程各量化一块 16 列块并直接写 FP4 bytes 和 scale byte，padding rows 完全不处理；二是 **packed BF16 rounding**：用 `cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32` 每次处理一对 rounding，减少单次 `F2F.BF16`+shift 的开销。作者强调输出与主分支 **bitwise identical**，无新参数。
- **与已有路线的差别**：不是新增 MoE 算法或量化方式，而只针对 CUDA 内核 epilogue 的 tile 形状与指令选择做优化，并声称对没有 `routing_weights` 的 kernel 零变化。
- **可信程度**：PR body 自报 GB300 上 full MoE call 延迟降低 1.16×–1.55×（M=1 到 32768），vLLM NVFP4 MoE serving 端到端输出吞吐 +5.9%；测试覆盖 bitwise 一致性、tile 阈值边界、CUDA graph replay。但这些是作者在特定硬件/配置下测得，独立复现尚未查证。
- **对 VLA 推理/GPU 系统启示**：VLA 骨干若采用 NVFP4 MoE，低 batch（机器人单步推理通常 batch 很小，甚至 M=1）时 padding 浪费最严重。这条 PR 说明：低精度 MoE 在机器人本地 GPU 上要真正低延迟，不能只看 GEMM 峰值，必须处理 epilogue 对 padding rows 的 ALU 绑架。对异步控制也有意义——若 VLA 需要高频动作修正，单次 MoE call 从 20.6µs 降到 17.3µs 仍有限，更值得借鉴的是“按有效行 compact 化 tile”的思路，避免无效计算进入热循环。

---

### 2. vLLM：Blackwell 上 QSA prefill 切换到 FlashInfer

- **原始材料**：[Perf][Qwen4Exp] Run QSA prefill steps with FlashInfer on Blackwell，2026-11-26，GitHub PR，https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69735。
- **试图解决的旧问题**：Qwen4Exp 的 QSA attention 在 B200 上占 8K prefill GPU 时间 26%。现有 Triton kernel 每次只处理一个 query row，导致每个 query row 单独加载已选中的 K/V blocks，K/V 加载无法跨相邻行共享。
- **核心技术机制**：在包含 prefill 的 step 中，使用 FlashInfer 的 `QToken-KvBlock-Sparse` kernel：一次处理一个 request 的 8 个相邻 query rows，对这 8 行的选中 block union 共享 K/V load；索引器输出和 attention 数学完全不变。decode-only step 仍保持 Triton kernel 在 FULL CUDA graphs 中，避免 decode 单请求时 FlashInfer 反而变慢（0.85×）。计划缓存按 `(layer, row bucket)` 复用，而非按请求形状 LRU，减少 host 开销。仅针对 SM100/SM103 BF16 KV。
- **与已有路线的差别**：此前 #55394/#56240 试图做类似替换，但前者在 GB10 上因 QSA 占比较低而关闭，后者跨 prefill/decode 且 footprint 约 1166 行。本 PR 只在 prefill 中启用 FlashInfer，约 360 行，**不改变 decode**。
- **可信程度**：PR body 提供 `vllm bench serve` 数据：median TTFT 降 8%–15%，prefill tok/s +11%–18%，production c32 输出吞吐 +4.2%，p99 TTFT −14%；QSA 层 kernel 路径 2.0–3.4×。质量无统计显著回归。有 repeated runs、GPU 顺序互换、prefix cache 重置控制。但仍是单一 B200、TP1 的自报数据，未独立验证。
- **对 VLA 推理/异步控制启示**：QSA 的“先选块、后按行组共享加载”与机器人 VLA 的时序注意力有同构性：多个未来动作 token 或相邻时间步的注意力通常共享相似的 KV 块。**对系统研究的启发是：稀疏注意力不应每个 query 独立规划，而应在行组层面共享 union，并保持 decode 路径的 CUDA graph 固定**，否则调度抖动会吃掉 kernel 收益。对机器人任务成功率/时间而言，VLA 首 token 延迟对应 prefill TTFT，QSA 优化若能降低长上下文场景的前端延迟，可能改善任务开始阶段的响应。

---

### 3. vLLM：Triton attention 中 per-token-head KV tile 向量化加载

- **原始材料**：[Perf][Attention] Vectorize per-token-head KV tile loads in Triton attention，2026-11-24，GitHub PR，https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69170。
- **试图解决的旧问题**：Triton attention kernel 读取 `int4_per_token_head`、`int8_per_token_head`、`fp8_per_token_head` 的低精度 KV cache 时，每次只加载 1 字节，造成内存带宽未充分利用。
- **核心技术机制**：在 kernel 发射时，从实际 strides 和 offsets 推断编译器可依赖的最宽对齐，然后按该宽度加载并 prefetch；例如 head size 128 时 K 读 8 字节、V 读 4 字节。只改变生成代码，不改变 KV cache 布局、page size、内存占用，与 layout 变更 PR 兼容。默认 BF16 路径不变。
- **与已有路线的差别**：不是改变 KV cache 存储格式，而是在现有布局上提升 load 指令宽度；与 #56081 同根因。总体 diff 仅 +78 −1。
- **可信程度**：PR body 提供 A100 和 RTX 5060 Ti 的 `vllm bench serve` 吞吐：Qwen3-14B int8 A100 prefill +33%、decode +34%；Qwen3-0.6B fp8 RTX 5060 Ti 两端均 +48%。输出 bytes 对 SHA256 bit-identical；GSM8K 分数无显著差异。数据方式较严谨，但仅为单个 PR 自报。
- **对 VLA 推理/GPU 系统启示**：低精度 KV cache（int4/int8/fp8）是降低显存与带宽的关键路径，但若 load 仍是 byte-per-instruction，低精度优势会大打折扣。**对端侧机器人 GPU 尤其重要**：VLA 在嵌入式设备上常以 int4/int8 KV 运行，向量化加载是一条低风险、不改内存布局的优化方向。对异步控制而言，decode 阶段带宽改善可稳定单步时延，减少因内存停顿造成的控制抖动。

---

### 4. vLLM：`sparse_disk` 后端——通过存储发布稀疏权重增量

- **原始材料**：[RL][Weight Transfer] Add sparse_disk backend for sparse deltas through storage，2026-11-26，GitHub PR，https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69112。
- **试图解决的旧问题**：在线强化学习/持续训练需要把稀疏权重变化传给推理副本，但 trainer 与 inference 可能不在一个 NCCL group，或需要喂养大量副本。现有 dense NCCL 需要共享通信组且接收缓冲受限于 GPU 内存；sparse NCCL 仍有通信组要求。
- **核心技术机制**：trainer 把每个版本的 patches 发布为一个文件到 storage；每个 inference worker 在 host memory 中保留自己那份 checkpoint 的副本（按 load plan 写出布局），更新时把新文件应用到 host 副本，再通过 load plan 把整个分片直接重载到模型，重新运行 post-load processing。patch 文件在写入 host copy 前逐 worker 校验。
- **与已有路线的差别**：相对 sparse NCCL，完全解耦 trainer 与 inference 的通信；相对 dense load plan，每个更新都是 full direct reload，复用已有 load plan 逻辑。Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 TP4 H20 上 reload 0.65–0.66s，3% 元素变化 2.98–3.48s；对比 sparse NCCL 2.0–2.4s，dense NCCL 0.74–0.90s。
- **可信程度**：PR body 提供 H20 端到端数据与 CPU unit tests；CI 不覆盖 GPU mapping、真实 TP layout、block FP8，因此这些部分仅作者验证。需谨慎看待实际部署中的 reload 时间。
- **对 VLA 推理/机器人启示**：这一路线与机器人持续学习、边缘-云端权重同步直接相关：**异步控制下权重更新不应阻塞推理**，通过 storage 广播 patch 是可行方向。但秒级 reload 时间远高于控制周期，只适用于批量更新（如夜间同步或低频率策略迭代）。对 VLA 系统来说，若要把 RL 在线学习部署到真实机器人，需要把 sparse_disk 式的解耦与可中断的权重重载结合，避免更新过程影响任务成功率或动作时间。

---

### 5. TensorRT-LLM：CPython 帧栈预留消除 executor host 抖动

- **原始材料**：[None][perf] Run the executor loop under a CPython frame-stack reserve，2026-11-25，GitHub PR，https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/22396。
- **试图解决的旧问题**：CPython 3.11+ 把帧放在 per-thread data-stack chunks；热调用若位于 chunk 边界，每次调用/返回都会 map/unmap 一个新 chunk。GB200 上每次 munmap 还会触发 Grace SMMU invalidation（一旦 NCCL peer-mapped memory 后）。作者报告 MiniMax-M3 piecewise CUDA graph prefill 的 host 时间约一半花在 munmap，造成毫秒级 executor step 开销。
- **核心技术机制**：新增 `run_with_frame_stack_reserve()`，在 import 时把 wrapper 的 `co_stacksize` 设为 65536，使 event loop 从大数据栈 chunk 的开始处运行，普通调用深度不会触达边界。仅对受影响 CPython 版本启用（3.11–3.13.13 之间、3.14–3.14.4 之间），可用 `TLLM_DISABLE_FRAME_STACK_RESERVE=1` 关闭。
- **与已有路线的差别**：与 sgl-torchtpu 的 PR 同技术；CPython 已在 3.13.13/3.14.4 修复，但 3.12 不会得到修复。这是 PyTorch executor 层面的通用改动，而非框架特有。
- **可信程度**：PR body 包含背景链接和 unit tests；但 QA 指出 executor wiring test 未列入任何 CI test list，且运行时 code object patch 依赖 CPython 内部细节，版本 gate 用 tuple 比较，backport patch 号变化会导致错误判断。因此该修复有效但工程上仍脆弱。
- **对 VLA 推理/机器人启示**：**这是今天材料中最容易被机器人控制社区忽略的信号**。机器人的异步控制闭环要求低抖动，但若 Python 运行时本身的 mmap/SMMU 行为在 GB200 这类 Grace-Hopper 系统上造成毫秒级暂停，即使 GPU kernel 再快也无法稳定。对 VLA 推理：更高频动作执行不应只关注 GPU 调度，还需限定 host Python 版本或避开 chunk 边界。这个发现提示：**端到端时延的最后一个毫秒，可能来自操作系统/解释器而非模型**。

---

### 跨领域弱信号

- **低精度 op 的 bitwise 可复现性**正成为工程默认要求：FlashInfer MoE 和 vLLM vectorized KV load 都明确验证输出 bit-identical，表明社区在低精度量化优化上开始把数值一致性作为前提条件。这对机器人部署至关重要，否则 VLA 任务成功率可能因不同优化路径的微小数值差异而变化。
- **稀疏注意力的 backend 替换正在形成范式**：vLLM QSA 从 Triton 到 FlashInfer 的切换，以及 llama.cpp 对 indexed bias Flash Attention 的移植（[b12801 release](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b12801)，2026-11-27，Release，仅 release notes，未验证性能），共同指向：未来稀疏/低精度 KV 的运行时可能由专用 kernel 主导，而不再只有通用 Triton。
- **权重热更新与推理引擎在解耦**：`sparse_disk` 和 `frame-stack reserve` 分别从权重传输和 host 运行时角度切入，说明在线学习基础设施正在下沉到推理引擎内部，而非仅靠外部编排。

### 趋势假设（含置信度与可反证实验）

1. **推理系统的下一版本收益来自 host 运行时与调度器，而不是 GEMM 峰值**。置信度：中高。可反证：若下一轮生产 benchmark 中 host 端优化（如 frame-stack reserve、计划缓存）带来的端到端吞吐提升 <3%，则该假设弱。  
2. **低精度 KV 与稀疏注意力将成为 VLA/长上下文推理的标准成本结构，且需要专用 kernel 协同**。置信度：中。可反证：若在机器人真实长上下文轨迹上，QSA 命中块稀疏度过低且 prefill TTFT 改善 <5%，则其在 VLA 上的适用性有限。  
3. **权重热更新将通过对象存储解耦 trainer 与 inference，但受限于秒级 reload，仅适用于批量策略更新而非高频控制**。置信度：高。可反证：若 `sparse_disk` 在 64+ replicas、10% 稀疏度下 reload 超 5s，或模型质量无法保证稀疏 patch 等价，则不适合作为 RL 异步控制后端。

### 本周值得精读的 2 篇

1. [vLLM QSA prefill on FlashInfer Blackwell](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69735) —— 稀疏注意力如何在保持 decode CUDA graph 不变的前提下获得 TTFT 收益，是 VLA 异步推理的实用模板。  
2. [FlashInfer NVFP4 MoE epilogue 优化](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9848) —— 展示低精度 MoE 在小 batch（M=1/8）时 epilogue 才是瓶颈，对机器人低延迟推理有直接参考价值。

---
**本次采集**：共采集 370 条，去重后 370 条；候选池 120 条，本次精选 6 条。源异常 1 处（见仓库 Actions 日志）。

selected.summary: ## 📌 Description In the routed NVFP4 MoE path that applies the routing weights before FC2 (pre-FC2, #9260), the gather GEMM1 epilogue (BF16-rounded ClampedReLU2, route weight, NVFP4 quantization of the FC2 input) is the per-tile bottleneck of GEMM1: - A GEMM1 tile costs a constant ≈5.4 µs at every M on GB300, whether 2 or 128 of its 128 rows hold routes, while GEMM2 streams the same weight bytes per expert at ≈3.5 µs per tile. GEMM1 runs at 3.07 TB/s, GEMM2 at 6.43 TB/s (ncu, M=96). - The epilogue is ALU/XU-bound: every epilogue warp sends its 32 TMEM rows × 128 columns through four single BF16 roundings (`F2F.BF16` + shifts), `tanh.approx` and `div.full`, for all 128 rows of the tile, including padding rows. `F2F.BF16` and `SHF` lead the epilogue stall samples. This PR makes that epilogue cheaper. There is no new argument or setting: it applies whenever the gather GEMM1 gets `routing_weights` (`routing_weights_before_fc2=True` in the CuTe-DSL fused MoE APIs). - **Compact decode tiles:** a tile with at most 64 valid rows stages `bf16(alpha * acc)` of its valid rows in the `sC` buffers; all 128 epilogue threads then quantize one 16-column block each and store the FP4 bytes and the scale byte directly. Padding rows are not processed. Tiles with more valid rows keep the per-subtile path. - **Packed BF16 rounding:** one `cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32` per pair of roundings, in both paths. **Behavior:** the same per-element operations in the same order, so the FP4 output and the scale factors of every valid row are bitwise identical to before. Padding rows of `out` / `out_scale` (rows of a tile past its `tile_idx_to_mn_limit`) may now be left unwritten; GEMM2 never stores padding rows. Kernels without `routing_weights` are unchanged: identical PTX and cubin to `main` for ClampedReLU2 and gated SwiGLU configurations (sm_103a). SM100/SM103 only, like the kernel. **Performance** (GB300, one full MoE call — routing sort, GEMM1, GEMM2 — in a CUDA graph, cold weights, µs, before → after, mean of two alternating runs). selected.summary: ## Overview The Triton attention kernels read per-token-head KV caches (`int4_per_token_head`, `int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`) one byte per load instruction. This PR works out, from the actual strides and offsets of the cache at launch, the widest alignment the compiler can rely on, and the kernels then load that many bytes per instruction, prefetched. At head size 128, for example, K is read 8 bytes and V 4 bytes at a time instead of 1. Only the generated kernel code changes. The KV cache memory layout, page size and memory use stay as they are, so this is independent of, and compatible with, the open PRs that change the layout (#62113, #56164). Same root cause as #56081. ## Claims - **Serving throughput goes up** for the per-token-head KV dtypes on `TRITON_ATTN`. `vllm bench serve`, total token throughput, mean of two runs per build, main -> this PR (terminal output below): - Qwen3-14B, int8, A100: 3536 -> 4701 tok/s (+33%) on 8192-token prefill, 2970 -> 3995 tok/s (+34%) with 256-token decode. - Qwen3-14B, int4, A100: 3641 -> 4214 tok/s (+16%) on 8192-token prefill, 3141 -> 3691 tok/s (+18%) with 256-token decode. - Qwen3-8B, int8, A100: 5586 -> 7624 tok/s (+36%) on 8192-token prefill, 4472 -> 6300 tok/s (+41%) with 256-token decode. - Qwen3-8B, int4, A100: 5822 -> 6386 tok/s (+10%) on 8192-token prefill, 4799 -> 5333 tok/s (+11%) with 256-token decode. - Qwen3-0.6B, fp8, RTX 5060 Ti: 9462 -> 13958 tok/s (+48%) on 8192-token prefill, 5884 -> 8730 tok/s (+48%) with 256-token decode. - **Accuracy is unchanged**: `lm_eval` GSM8K, of the 16 main/PR score pairs, 14 differ by no more than the reported stderr. The largest gap is -0.0228 (Qwen3-0.6B fp8); a repeat of both builds gives +0.0083, and two runs of the same build differ by up to 0.0159 (terminal output below). - **Kernel output is bit-identical to main**: with the same inputs, the raw output bytes have the same sha256 on main and on this PR for every kernel call checked (72 on the RTX 5060 Ti, 48 on the A100), including the engine's interleaved layout, where main loads byte by byte and this PR 8 and 4 bytes at a time. - **Small diff**: +78 -1 in 3 files, test included. - **No layout, page-size or memory change, and no new option.** The default (bf16) KV cache takes the unchanged code path. ## Validation Builds: main `cc00267752`, this PR `bb50346e57`. selected.summary: ## Overview Adds `sparse_disk`, a weight transfer backend for sparse weight deltas published through storage, for trainers that cannot share an NCCL group with inference or that feed many replicas. The trainer publishes each version's patches as one file. Every inference worker keeps its part of the checkpoint in host memory, laid out as its load plan writes it. In an update, the worker applies the new files to that copy and copies its whole part into the model, so every update is a full direct reload through the load plan, with post-load processing rerun. ## Claims - Sparse updates without an NCCL group between trainer and inference; every replica reads the same patch files. - No new loading pattern: each update is a full direct reload, as dense NCCL with `use_load_plan` does. After `start_reload`, planned tensors are copied to the load plan's destinations and marked loaded, the names the plan leaves out go through `model.load_weights()`, and `finish_reload` reruns post-load processing. Configurations no load plan supports are refused at init; a model whose loads cannot be planned fails at the first update, which is sent before serving. Tested on a BF16 and a block-FP8 checkpoint (below). - Pause on Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, TP4, H20: - 0.65–0.66 s to reload a version; - 0.90–1.73 / 1.47–1.77 / 2.98–3.48 s with 0.1 / 1 / 3 % of elements changed. For comparison, on the same node: 2.0–2.4 s for sparse NCCL and 0.74–0.90 s for dense NCCL with a load plan. Dense NCCL ran with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`; at the default, its 1 GiB receive buffer did not fit. - Each worker validates a patch file before writing that file's changes to its host copy. Restarted servers rebuild their copy from the startup checkpoint and replay the published files. - A new engine file, its registration and docs; no core files change. ## Validation Unit tests (CPU, on 8bd378f2b6): pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k sparse_disk 6 passed, 168 deselected, 1 warning in 1.22s The six tests run on CPU; in CI they are in the optional nightly H100 Distributed Features job. CI does not exercise GPU mapping, pinned transfers, real tensor-parallel layouts or block FP8 (the last two need checkpoints it doesn't have); the H20 runs below did. - `test_sparse_disk_updates_equal_a_cold_start_on_the_patched_checkpoint_cpu`: the model ends bit for bit equal to a cold start on the densely patched checkpoint in each of these cases: - after the trainer's sends; - on a reload after the weights were lost; - on a restarted server that replays the files; - on a server started from a newer checkpoint, with the file it already contains deleted. It also checks that a re-init with another `base_version`, an update older than the model (also after a rebuild that stopped partway), and a second publish of a version are refused. The toy model covers tensor-parallel halves along both dims, a tensor split over two parameters, a 0-dim tensor, a name the load plan leaves to `load_weights` (its loader changes its input in place), a name the model skips, three dtypes, and patches cut across chunks. - `test_sparse_disk_bad_file_is_refused_before_any_write_cpu`: a file with one bad patch is refused before it writes the host copy, and a new update to the last version restores the model. The bad patch has an unknown name, a wrong shape or dtype, an index repeated across a chunk boundary, or an out-of-range index. The two follow-up commits, ea337843fb and 8bd378f2b6, add refusals and version checks, clean up a failed publish, check patch names against the tensors the default loader yields, and trim the code. They do not change how a file is mapped, written or loaded, so the end-to-end runs below still apply. End to end on 8×H20 in one node, with a concurrency-32 completion load running. E

selected.title: [NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM PR] [None][perf] Run the executor loop under a CPython frame-stack reserve
selected.summary: CPython 3.11+ keeps frames in per-thread data-stack chunks. When a hot call sits at a chunk boundary, every call maps a fresh chunk and every return unmaps it (gh-142183). On GB200 each munmap also pays a Grace SMMU invalidation once NCCL has peer-mapped memory, so the churn costs milliseconds per executor step: MiniMax-M3 piecewise CUDA graph prefill steps spent about half their host time in munmap, all on the executor thread. CPython fixed this in 3.13.13 and 3.14.4; 3.12 will not get the fix. Add run_with_frame_stack_reserve() and call PyExecutor.event_loop through it, so the loop starts near the beginning of a large data-stack chunk and ordinary call depths never reach a boundary. The reserve is applied only on affected CPython versions and can be disabled with TLLM_DISABLE_FRAME_STACK_RESERVE=1. Cover the version gate, the disable switch, the churn itself and the executor wiring with cpu_only unit tests.
